 GST reforms take effect, offering businesses relief on discounts and refunds
 India's GST reforms promise easier seller registration, faster refunds and simpler compliance, but raise questions over implementation costs. 
 Smruthi Nadig 
 ETEntrepreneur 
 Updated On Nov 3, 2026 at 12:08 PM IST
 Copy Link

 Share on Facebook
 India's revised GST framework aims to simplify compliance, accelerate refunds, and ease tax administration for businesses. 
The Centre has rolled out a fresh set of goods and services tax (GST) changes from November 1, following recommendations made at the 57th GST Council meeting on October 8.
The Finance Ministry notified key amendments on October 26 under the Finance Act, 2026. These ease the conditions for claiming tax benefits on post-supply discounts, expand refund eligibility for businesses operating under an inverted duty structure, and introduce faster, system-based processing of eligible refund claims.
 Separate procedural changes also simplify GST registration for small sellers using e-commerce platforms. The earlier framework required discounts to be established through an agreement entered into at or before the time of supply and linked to relevant invoices.
The reforms widen the scope of refunds under the inverted duty structure, where tax paid on inputs exceeds the tax applicable on finished goods. Eligible input service tax credit availed from November 1 can now be included in refund claims.
 The system will also provide for 90 per cent provisional refunds for eligible claims involving inverted duty structures and zero-rated supplies, subject to risk assessment.
 The simplified registration framework for small e-commerce sellers has drawn support. Amazon said the GST Council’s recommendations on registration, principal place of business requirements and input tax credit could bring greater certainty to small businesses. The company said its marketplace had more than 20 lakh sellers, over 70 per cent of whom were based in tier-II and tier-III cities.
 “We appreciate the Government's responsiveness to the concerns of sellers and look forward to continuing to work together towards a GST framework that enables more entrepreneurs and small businesses to thrive,” an Amazon spokesperson told ETEntrepreneur .
 Meesho also welcomed the Council’s recommendations, saying easier registration and faster refunds could help sellers expand their reach and improve working capital.
 “The proposed GST framework for delivery services is also a step towards greater clarity and uniformity,” a Meesho spokesperson said.
However, implementation concerns remain around the separate change to the GST treatment of e-commerce delivery services. Ahead of the reform taking effect, NASSCOM sought a deferment until January 1, 2027, saying the revised 5 per cent GST rate without ITC would require changes to enterprise resource planning, invoicing, tax calculations and compliance systems.
